newsitem.title: FRANCE: Gas is next century's "fuel of choice" - BP.
newsitem.headline: Gas is next century's "fuel of choice" - BP.

text.p: Natural gas has the potential to become the next century's "fuel of choice" in Europe, John Browne, group chief executive of British Petroleum Co Plc told a conference on Thursday.
Speaking at the Gas Executive Summit Conference, Browne outlined four ways in which the gas industry is reshaping.

"First is the enhancement of supply. There is plenty of gas. New supplies are coming onstream very fast. And the range of suppliers with long-range infrastructures is adding to the security of supply."

"Improved efficiency and lower turbine costs have brought down the cost of power generation. Since 1990, in the U.K. 11 gigawatts of electricity from gas have opened, and another 10 gigawatts are planned for the next five years. In 1990, gas plants produced one percent of the U.K.'s electricity. The figure is now 26 percent.
Browne identified political integration of Europe and the development of the single market as a third decisive factor.
"The principles of the single market are filtering through to the energy sector. We have had an electricity directive and now serious work is being done on the gas directive.
"The opening of national markets to competition is also happening. In our experience, competition is a very effective way to stimulate demand and get consumers to switch to gas."

But Browne added that for him the strongest stimulus to the growth of gas is consumer pressure. Apart from the environmental benefits of gas, Browne sees demand coming from industrial consumers who need competitively priced fuel as the debate over Europe's competitiveness in global terms, grows.
"The reshaping of the European industry is only just beginning, he said

He told the conference that BP has several interests in gas: as a North sea producer selling 10 billion cubic meters a year; through its rapidly growing arm BP Gas; as the holder of 25.5 percent of German distributor Ruhrgas; as a 10 percent owner of the Anglo-Belgium Interconnector pipeline; and through its joint venture with Algerian state oil company Sonatrach in the In-Salah project.
